central_invariant: After a trusted-side revocation of the exact frozen Task15 request SHA durably commits to the same SQLite database used for single-use dispatch, no subsequent mock dispatch claim may be made for that request, even with a valid copied TEST Ed25519 grant and stolen synthetic HMAC session key.
key_risk_truth: Before the revoke transaction commits, an attacker with BOTH session key and valid signed grant can win the first already-authorized mock effect. Post-claim revocation cannot undo that effect.
revocation_trigger: Trusted-side direct method only; no worker IPC revocation endpoint. Authorization to invoke trusted method is assumed, not independently proven.
serialization_boundary: SQLite BEGIN IMMEDIATE lock guards revocation lookup + insert of DISPATCH_UNKNOWN in same transaction; trusted revoke uses same SQLite BEGIN IMMEDIATE
persistence: SQLite revoked_requests and revocation_audit tables; duplicate revoke idempotent; no reopening/reset if ledger missing
frozen_request_sha_scope: sha256 canonical exact_request from Task15 mock-only core; does not cover full native AgentDojo wire body
session_key: synthetic key assumed stolen; no mitigation for key extraction, same-process code, or host-level compromise
assumptions: Host/broker trust boundary, SQLite file and filesystem permissions remain uncompromised
Local trusted-side revocation call is controlled by operator but independently enrolled authorization is out of scope
Mock sink executes no HTTP and never uses real Provider API key
Clock and test signer are local synthetic fixtures
No worker container integration: this proves broker core transaction only
explicit_nonclaims: Does not prevent stolen key and valid signed grant from consuming the one allowed action before revocation
Does not revoke already-claimed in-flight or already-recorded mock effects
Does not automatically rotate session keys or prevent stealing them again
Does not prove OS process isolation, authenticated IPC revocation operations, or full native wire authenticity
Does not authorize real Provider requests/billing or bank effects
next: Integrate broker-only trusted revocation authority and same-DB transaction into a separately audited Docker Unix-IPC scenario; test adverse ordering. Keep Provider live blocked.
